name: Radish (mooli)
model: written by hand (Claude) from the Urdu KB

aspects.overview: Radish (mooli) is a root vegetable of the mustard (crucifer) family, first grown in China. In Pakistan it is grown on about 10,133 hectares, producing about 173,806 tonnes. It is mostly a winter crop, eaten raw in salad or cooked, and contains phosphorus, calcium, iron and vitamin C. It likes cool weather; September and October are the best months, when every variety can be sown. Choose the variety by its sowing time, your soil and your area, otherwise yield and root quality fall. Early radish is grown on fertile land close to a river, canal or watercourse.
aspects.varieties:
Varieties by sowing time:
40-Din Wali (40-day): sow July and August; tolerates heat; ready in 40 to 55 days.
Mooli Mino: sow September and October; ready in 55 to 60 days; high yield and can stay longer in the field.
Green Neck: sow September and October; ready in 55 to 60 days; very good taste.
Lal Pari: sow October and November; tolerates cold; good for salad; ready in 60 to 75 days.
All Season: sow November to mid December; tolerates cold; can stay longer in the field; ready in 60 to 70 days.
Seed rate: early crop 3 to 5 kg per acre for dibbling (chopa) or line sowing (kera), 4 to 5 kg per acre for broadcasting (chhatta). Main-season crop: 3 to 3.5 kg per acre with either method.
aspects.sowing:
Land: plough deep once, or normal plough twice, then level the field completely, with laser levelling if possible; uneven land wastes water and lowers germination and yield. Mix 10 to 15 tonnes of well-rotted farmyard manure per acre while preparing the land, then make the soil soft and fine with planking or a rotavator.
Sowing: sow on both sides of 75 cm (2.5 foot) ridges. Divide the field into plots of about 1 kanal so water can be applied evenly.
Dibbling (chopa): 1 to 2 seeds per spot, 6 to 7 cm apart, on both sides of the ridge.
Line sowing (kera): smooth the ridge top, make lines 1 to 1.5 cm deep on both sides, and drop one seed every 2 to 3 cm. Mix seed with silt or sand so it spreads evenly.
Broadcasting (chhatta): spread half the seed along the field and half across it, then make ridges with a ridger and divide into plots.
Thinning: when the third or fourth leaf appears, keep one healthy plant every 5 to 6 cm and remove the rest, as early as possible; timely thinning gives thick, good-looking roots. In the July–August crop, thin once the plants are established, because heat can kill some plants.
Seed rate: early crop 3 to 5 kg per acre (dibbling or line sowing) or 4 to 5 kg (broadcast); main-season crop 3 to 3.5 kg per acre.
aspects.fertilizer:
Farmyard manure: 10 to 15 tonnes of well-rotted manure per acre during land preparation.
At sowing (after land preparation, before making ridges), main-season crop: 1 bag DAP (9 kg nitrogen, 23 kg phosphorus) and 1 bag sulphate of potash (25 kg potash) per acre. Potash is very important for root crops.
Early crop: use 1.5 bags sulphate of potash (34.5 kg potash) per acre; it keeps the soil soft and protects the crop from high heat.
When roots start forming (about 20 to 25 days after sowing in the early crop, 25 to 40 days in the main-season crop): half a bag of urea (11.5 kg nitrogen) per acre. Also give half a bag of urea per acre after the second hoeing.
aspects.irrigation: First irrigation right after sowing, very carefully: keep the water 6 to 7 cm below the seed line so only moisture reaches the seed. If water goes over the ridges the surface crusts, germination drops, plant numbers fall and roots form badly. Method: apply water once below the seed line, then after one or two hours, when most has soaked in, apply the same amount again so moisture reaches the ridge tops. Divide the field into plots of about 1 kanal for even watering.
aspects.pests_diseases:
Pests: mealybug, aphid and armyworm (lashkari sundi).
Armyworm: spray Timer 1.9 EC at 200 ml per acre.
Mealybug and aphid: spray Crown or Launcher 200 SL at 250 ml per acre.
Diseases: radish is usually free of disease, but in early sowing or certain weather the leaves can get leaf spot. Spray Score (difenoconazole 25 EC) at 120 ml per acre.
Safety: do not hoe the field right after a spray.
aspects.weeds:
Main weeds: itsit, wild amaranth (jangli cholai), lamb grass, purslane (kulfa), wild halon and wild spinach.
Give at least two hoeings to control weeds; after the second hoeing apply half a bag of urea per acre.
It is usually better not to use weedicides: they often make roots near the soil surface shrink, which lowers the market price.
If chemical control is needed: spray Top 330 or Rebor 33 EC at 10 ml per litre of water within 1 to 2 days of sowing, with a flat-fan nozzle. The spray can affect root shape.
Do not hoe right after spraying: it breaks the weedicide layer so weeds come back, and dust can carry the chemical into the farmer's body and lungs.
aspects.harvesting: Harvest by variety: the early 40-day radish forms roots fast and should be pulled within 45 to 50 days. Later varieties such as Mino, Green Neck and Lal Pari can stay longer but must be harvested before 70 to 80 days, otherwise flowering starts and the market price falls. If harvest of early varieties is late, the roots become hollow inside and sell for less.
aspects.machinery: Plough deep once or normal plough twice, then level completely; laser levelling is best. Use a ridger to make ridges and a rotavator or planking to make the soil soft and fine.
aspects.other: Cost per acre on own land: about 33,000 rupees (land preparation 7,000; seed 1,000; fertilizer 10,000; water 2,000; weed control 2,000; pests and diseases 1,500; harvesting 4,500; transport 5,000). Average income is about 85,000 rupees per acre, so the crop is profitable.

timing.sowing: July to mid December, by variety (best September to October)
timing.harvesting: 40 to 80 days after sowing, by variety
